s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute neurological syndrome with fluctuating cognitive and focal neurological deficits
salient_findings: Mild headache and right facial droop
Extensive white matter changes on MRI
key_facts: History of well-controlled hypertension and hyperlipidemia
On methotrexate and sulfasalazine treatment
Developed mild aphasia and confusion lasting several hours
Right leg weakness resolved within 2 days
Presented with mild headache and right facial droop
Neurological examination revealed paraphasic errors and word-finding difficulty
Mild right nasolabial flattening and bilateral upgoing plantars
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein level
High titer of cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody
CSF analysis showed 12/µL white blood cell count and 4 oligoclonal bands
MRI Brain showed extensive white matter changes with enhancement along the arachnoid surface
Brain biopsy showed thick exudate in subarachnoid space with lymphocytes and plasma cells

shortlist.label: Multiple Sclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: Subacute neurological syndrome with fluctuating cognitive and focal neurological deficits, elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein level, and presence of oligoclonal bands in CSF

shortlist.label: Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder
shortlist.why_kept: History of optic neuritis and transverse myelitis, presence of aquaporin-4 antibodies not mentioned but clinical presentation and CSF findings are consistent

shortlist.label: Central Nervous System Vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Subacute neurological syndrome with fluctuating cognitive and focal neurological deficits, presence of inflammation in CSF and brain biopsy, but no evidence of vasculitis

shortlist.label: Hashimoto Encephalopathy
shortlist.why_kept: History of autoimmune disease, presence of high titer of cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody, and subacute neurological syndrome with fluctuating cognitive and focal neurological deficits

shortlist.label: Granulomatous Meningoencephalitis of Unknown Etiology
shortlist.why_kept: Brain biopsy showed thick exudate in subarachnoid space with lymphocytes and plasma cells, and presence of multinucleated giant cells, consistent with granulomatous inflammation

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of mild aphasia, confusion, and right leg weakness, along with the findings of elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate, high titer of cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody, and CSF analysis showing 12/µL white blood cell count and 4 oligoclonal bands, suggests an inflammatory process. The brain biopsy showing thick exudate in the subarachnoid space with lymphocytes and plasma cells, and the MRI findings of extensive white matter changes with enhancement along the arachnoid surface, are consistent with granulomatous meningoencephalitis. The absence of evidence for vasculitis, tuberculosis, or fungal infection, and the lack of a clear alternative diagnosis, supports this choice.

rejected.label: Multiple Sclerosis
rejected.why: The presence of granulomatous changes on biopsy and the pattern of enhancement on MRI are not typical for multiple sclerosis.

rejected.label: Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and biopsy findings do not specifically suggest neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder, and the absence of aquaporin-4 antibody testing results makes this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Central Nervous System Vasculitis
rejected.why: The biopsy did not show evidence of vasculitis, making this diagnosis unlikely.

rejected.label: Hashimoto Encephalopathy
rejected.why: There is no mention of thyroid disease or antibodies suggestive of Hashimoto's, making this diagnosis less likely.
